clinician.final_diagnosis: bone marrow biopsy showed diffuse bone marrow replacement by metastatic adenocarcinoma (Fig. 1). PSA stain was consistent with tumor cells of prostatic origin (Fig. 2).
clinician.trajectory_summary: An 86-year-old man presented with progressive dyspnea, fatigue, and palpitations over one month. Labs revealed markedly elevated PSA with previously normal levels. Bone scintigraphy showed probable metastases. Bone marrow biopsy confirmed diffuse marrow replacement by metastatic adenocarcinoma with PSA immunostaining confirming prostatic origin. Treatment with docetaxel, leuprolide, and zolendronic acid was initiated but with no significant symptom improvement after four cycles. Subsequently, palliative care was started with hemotransfusion support.
